# Oaks Rough Draft Analysis

```{r}
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

```{r}
# read in data
Height_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Seedling Heights")

Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")
LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",              
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

LICOR_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",  
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES,
             col_types = "text")


ALL_Licor_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

ALL_Licor <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = ALL_Licor_NAMES, 
             col_types = "text")

LICOR_Data_Raw <- full_join(LICOR_Data_Raw, ALL_Licor)
```

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
# Clean LICOR data for ANOVA
LICOR_Data <- LICOR_Data_Raw |> 
  select(SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD, `USERDEF_Block Number_NA`, `USERDEF_Tag Number_NA`, Treatment_NA_NA, Sapling_AB_etc_NA_NA, Dead_Alive_NA_NA, `PORO_gsw_mol+1m-2s-1`) |> 
  
# Rename columns
  rename(Date = SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD, 
         Block = `USERDEF_Block Number_NA`, 
         Tag = `USERDEF_Tag Number_NA`, 
         Treatment = Treatment_NA_NA,
         Sapling_ID = Sapling_AB_etc_NA_NA, 
         Status = Dead_Alive_NA_NA,
         GSW = `PORO_gsw_mol+1m-2s-1`) |> 
  
# Remove 'dead' saplings 
  filter(Status != "Dead" )

# Checking classes of variables, changing to what they need to be for analysis

class(LICOR_Data$GSW)
class(LICOR_Data$Treatment)

LICOR_Data$GSW <- as.numeric(LICOR_Data$GSW)
LICOR_Data$Treatment <- as.factor(LICOR_Data$Treatment)

LICOR_Data$Date <- as.character(LICOR_Data$Date)

```

```{r}
# Clean moisture data and combine with LICOR data for regression

# Select what columns I want
Moist_Data <- Moist_Data_Raw |> 
  select(Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc) |> 
  # remove NA rows
  na.omit() |> 
  
  # rename columns
  rename(VWC_1 = VWC1_perc, 
         VWC_2 = VWC2_perc, 
         VWC_3 = VWC3_perc)

# change classes of columns 
Moist_Data$VWC_1 <- as.numeric(Moist_Data$VWC_1)
Moist_Data$VWC_2 <- as.numeric(Moist_Data$VWC_2)
Moist_Data$VWC_3 <- as.numeric(Moist_Data$VWC_3)

Moist_Data$Block <- as.factor(Moist_Data$Block)
Moist_Data$Treatment <- as.factor(Moist_Data$Treatment)

# create a mean colum for VWC
Moist_Data <- Moist_Data |> 
  mutate(VWC_mean = rowMeans(pick(VWC_1, VWC_2, VWC_3), na.rm = TRUE)) 

# join LICOR and moisture data 
LICOR_Moist_DATA<- full_join(Moist_Data, LICOR_Data, by = c("Treatment", "Block"), relationship = "many-to-many")
```

## ANOVA

Does treatment influence stomatal conductance of Oak seedlings?

### Checking for Normality and Assumptions

```{r}
# assumption/normality tests

# visualizing stomatal conductance across treatments 
ggplot(LICOR_Data)+
  aes(x = Treatment, y = GSW,)+
  geom_boxplot()

# removing two obvious outliers
LICOR_Graphing <- LICOR_Data[-c(72, 73), ]

ggplot(LICOR_Graphing)+
  aes(x = Treatment, y = GSW,)+
  geom_boxplot()

# exmaining distribution
ggplot(LICOR_Graphing)+
  aes(x = GSW)+
  geom_histogram()
# data appears normal

# write the model 
anova_model <- lm(GSW ~ Treatment, data = LICOR_Graphing)

# checking q-q residuals
plot(anova_model, which = 2)
# the majority of the residuals follow the trendline, so I will continue

# shapiro test
shapiro.test(anova_model$residuals)
# W = 0.86233, p-value = 5.643e-13
# this indicates abnormality (p < 0.05) in the data, but this test is highly sensitive with large sample sizes so I will continue

# testing for homogeneity of variance 
plot(anova_model, 1)
# the residuals are highly variable, so I might try removing more outliers and/or transforming the data

# Some outliers keep getting pointed out
LICOR_anova <- LICOR_Graphing[-c(2, 66, 67), ]

anova_model2 <- lm(GSW ~ Treatment, data = LICOR_anova)

plot(anova_model2, which = 2)
# this plot looks better, the residuals follow a more linear path
plot(anova_model2, 1)
# this plot looks slightly better, but there is still heterogeneity of variances, I will do a bartlett test

# bartlett test
bartlett.test(GSW ~ Treatment, data = LICOR_anova)
# Bartlett's K-squared = 40.714, df = 4, p-value = 3.08e-08
# p-value is extremely low, indicating variance between treatments, I will now try to transform the data 

# transform data to see if that helps normality and HOV
anova_model3 <- lm(log(GSW) ~ Treatment, data = LICOR_anova)

plot(anova_model3, which = 2)
plot(anova_model3, 1)
# both plots look worse than the untransformed data, so I will run the ANOVA as welch's since there is unequal variances among groups 
```

### One-Way Welch's ANOVA (Unequal Variances)

```{r}
# Running Welch's ANOVA

oneway.test(GSW ~ Treatment, data = LICOR_anova, var.equal = FALSE)

# F = 1.8511, num df = 4.000, denom df = 15.254, p-value = 0.1708
# There is no need for post hoc testing as the result is statistically insignificant
```

### Figure

```{r}

ggplot(LICOR_anova)+
  aes(x = Treatment, y = GSW, color = Treatment)+
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5)+
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7)+
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = 0.15, label = "Welch's ANOVA, p-value = 0.1708", fontface = "bold")+
  ylab("Stomatal Conductance (mmol m −2 s −1)")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  ggtitle("Stomatal conductance of oak seedlings across treatments")

# I created a boxplot with a jitter to show the means of each group mapped against the variance.  
```

## Regression

Is greater stomatal conductance associated with an increase in soil moisture for oak seedlings?

### Checking for Normality and Assumptions

```{r}
# I know how the LICOR data behaves, but I must now look at the soil moisture data

# First, I need to remove the intial outliers
LICOR_Moist_Graphing <- LICOR_Moist_DATA[-c(94, 95), ]

# How is the soil moisture data distributed?
ggplot(LICOR_Moist_Graphing)+
  aes(VWC_mean)+
  geom_histogram(bins = 20)
# The data appears abonormal, possibly with bimodal distribution. Sampling date may play a role in this distribution. I will separate the data by date. 
ggplot(LICOR_Moist_Graphing)+
  aes(VWC_mean)+
  geom_histogram(bins = 25)+
  facet_wrap(~Date)
# The data shows a sharper left-skewed distribution on the first (dry) date, and a more gradual right-skewed distribution on the second (post-rain) date 

# I will try log-transforming the data 
ggplot(LICOR_Moist_Graphing)+
  aes(log(VWC_mean))+
  geom_histogram()
# This is still skewed, but now only to one side instead of bimodal

# I will see if there is a linear relationship between the two intended variables
ggplot(LICOR_Moist_Graphing) +
  aes(x = VWC_mean, y = GSW)+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

ggplot(LICOR_Moist_Graphing) +
  aes(x = log(VWC_mean), y = GSW)+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

# Create the model
LICOR_Moist_model <- lm(GSW ~ VWC_mean, data = LICOR_Moist_Graphing)

plot(LICOR_Moist_model, which = 2)
plot(LICOR_Moist_model, 1)

# Log-transform VWC data 
LICOR_Moist_Reg <- LICOR_Moist_Graphing %>% mutate(log_VWC = log(VWC_mean))
LICOR_Moist_Reg[is.na(LICOR_Moist_Reg) | LICOR_Moist_Reg == "Inf" | LICOR_Moist_Reg == "-Inf"] <- NA

LICOR_Moist_model2 <- lm(GSW ~ log_VWC, data = LICOR_Moist_Reg)
plot(LICOR_Moist_model2, which = 2)
plot(LICOR_Moist_model2, 1)
# the HOV looks better in the original model, so I will not transform the data

```

### Spearman's Rank Test 

```{r}

# Is there a correlation between the variables?
LICOR_Moist_Spear <- cor.test(LICOR_Moist_Graphing$GSW, LICOR_Moist_Graphing$VWC_mean, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

LICOR_Moist_Spear$estimate
rho_spear <- round(LICOR_Moist_Spear$estimate, 3)

LICOR_Moist_Spear$p.value
round(LICOR_Moist_Spear$p.value, 3)
# rho = -0.257, p-value = 0.001
# there is a significant negative correlation between GSW and VWC 

```

### Simple Linear Regression

```{r}

summary(LICOR_Moist_model)

slope <- coef(LICOR_Moist_model)[2]
int <- coef(LICOR_Moist_model)[1]
p <- summary(LICOR_Moist_model)$coefficients[2, 4]
Rsq <- summary(LICOR_Moist_model)$r.squared

Rsq <- round(Rsq, 4)
slope <- round(slope, 4)
int <- round(int, 4)
p <- round(p, 6)

```

### Figure

```{r}

Reg_plot <- ggplot(LICOR_Moist_Graphing) +
  aes(x = VWC_mean, y = GSW)+
  geom_point()
  

Reg_plot +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  geom_text(x = 10, y = 0.15,
            label = paste("R-squared = ", Rsq, "\n", 
                          "y = ", slope, "x +", int,"\n", "p =", p)) +
  ylab("Stomatal Conductance (mmol m −2 s −1)")+
  xlab("Soil Moisture (%VWC)")+
  ggtitle("Oak Seedling Stomatal Conductance vs Soil Moisture")
```
